analysis: What changed vs the 6 AM brief: the rebound opened as advertised — Dow +1%, S&P +1.2%, Nasdaq +1.6% at the bell per Barron's — then gave back roughly half the gain inside 30 minutes, and the driver was the same name leading the rebound. Nvidia opened +1.7% at $151.90, then flipped to -1.9% (~$146.58 by 9:54 AM ET) after a Bloomberg report, flagged by MarketWatch as the possible trigger, that some newer Blackwell chips were used at a China data center tied to a woman Huang had an affair with. That report is single-source and unconfirmed by Nvidia, so treat the trigger as fragile — but the price action itself is confirmed by MarketWatch, IBD, Cointime and Finnhub, and it cut the Nasdaq's gain from +1.6% to +0.8%. The rest of the Mag 7 held up: Meta +2.5% at $625.12 led the group, and Tesla and Anthropic (back above its $83 IPO price near $89) were early winners per IBD. The Melius upgrade of Nvidia to Buy with a $220 target, from $185, is a counterweight, but it landed before the reversal and did not hold the stock. Bitcoin slipping below $60,000 while gold holds +4% near $3,708 keeps the risk picture mixed rather than cleanly risk-on. Signal vs noise: the NVDA reversal and the fading of opening gains are signal — the rebound's lead name is still the market's pressure point and thin half-day liquidity is amplifying the swing. The Bloomberg affair-tied datacenter claim is noise risk until a second source or Nvidia confirms it. The premarket rotation story (memory/optical ripping, staples down ~1%) still stands; nothing in the first 30 minutes overturned it, but the session's durability now hinges on whether Nvidia stabilizes into the 1 PM ET close.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Stocks opened sharply higher on the Black Friday half-day session, then pared about half the gain in the first 30 minutes: at 9:44 AM ET the Dow was 50,563.50 (+0.76%), the S&P 500 7,238.26 (+0.77%) and the Nasdaq 23,758.47 (+0.73%), after futures had pointed to +1.45%, +1.7% and +2.4%. Barron's had the Nasdaq +1.6% at the open; MarketWatch says it faded to +0.8% after Nvidia flipped red.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rebound is holding, but the fade off the open on a 3.5-hour session shows how thin holiday liquidity amplifies moves in both directions.

headlines.headline: Nvidia opened +1.7% at $151.90, then quickly reversed to -1.9% in recent trading (~$146.58 at 9:54 AM ET per Finnhub, intraday low $145.39) after being +4.7% premarket. MarketWatch points to a Bloomberg report that some newer Blackwell chips were used at a data center in China tied to a woman CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with. Earnings context: Q3 FY2027 reported Nov 17, EPS $2.68 on revenue $115.844B.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rebound's lead name flipping red within 25 minutes of the open took the shine off the whole tech rally — and the Bloomberg report behind it is single-source, unconfirmed by Nvidia, so treat that trigger as fragile.

headlines.headline: Melius Research upgraded Nvidia to Buy from Hold this week, raising its price target to $220 from $185, per Invezz. The upgrade followed Monday's 31.5% jump on Huang's reinstatement as CEO and the Q3 beat, and came before Friday's intraday reversal.
headlines.why_it_matters: A major broker moving to Buy with a higher target is a sentiment tailwind for the name — but it did not hold the stock through the morning's reversal, so the upgrade alone is not the tape's driver today.

headlines.headline: Meta led the Mag 7 in early trading, +2.50% at $625.12 as of 9:52 AM ET (open $628.39, high $630.09, low $620.80 vs Wednesday's $609.89 close). Earnings context: Q3 FY2026 reported Oct 21, EPS $7.40 on revenue $64.601B.
headlines.why_it_matters: Meta holding a ~2.5% gain while Nvidia flipped red shows the rebound is not a single-stock story — the rest of the Mag 7 is still carrying the tape.

headlines.headline: Tesla, Anthropic and SpaceX were early winners at the open, per IBD's live coverage. Anthropic traded back above its $83 IPO price at around $89 (+~8%), per CoinDesk via a market brief, after slipping below the IPO price earlier in the week.
headlines.why_it_matters: Freshly listed and high-beta names leading the tape alongside the Mag 7 is what a risk-on holiday session looks like — breadth beyond the index heavyweights.

headlines.headline: Bitcoin fell below $60,000 in early trading, down 1.35% over 24 hours, per Cointime's live feed, after closing the prior session near $61,670.
headlines.why_it_matters: Crypto giving back ground while equities rally and gold holds +4% keeps the risk picture mixed — not a clean risk-on signal across asset classes.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. Carry-forward: Q3 2026 (Nov 3) revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y) beat the ~$344.7M consensus and adjusted EPS $0.33 beat the $0.26 consensus; adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M and DCF to $495-505M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6. Leverage 3.78x, near the 3.75x target; $600M of 6.75% senior notes due 2035 issued in September. Zacks raised FY2026 EPS estimate to $1.16 from $1.04 (Nov 24) and holds a Hold rating; a Nov 24 Zacks piece frames the growth case — $500M order book through 2029, >60% of 2027 new horsepower contracted, record $23.14/month revenue per horsepower (+8% y/y) — while a Nov 26 Seeking Alpha Hold note counters with limited upside at 8.29x forward EV/EBITDA amid substantial debt, against a Nov 25 buy-rated piece at $23.63 citing the 8.9% yield and 1.67x coverage. USAC opened Wednesday at $23.04. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027.
